svg.text: Keeping key order: what moves on an insertion or a deletion
A conventional node keeps descriptors sorted and shifts them to open or close a gap. V1 keeps descriptors in fixed slots and shifts only the one-byte slot indices of order[].
Leaf descriptor in v1: RangeRef 24 B + cv 8 B = 32 B. Capacity 8 here; v1 leaves hold 59 entries. Highlighted cells are the bytes written or moved by the operation.
V1: fixed slots + occupied bitmap + order[]
same six entries; physical placement is arbitrary, order[] gives the sorted sequence
Insert coconut (rank 3, between cherry and date)
shift date, fig, grape one slot right: 3 descriptors × 32 B = 96 B moved, then write 32 B
write the descriptor into free slot 3 (32 B), set its bit, shift three order bytes: 3 B moved
shift cherry … grape one slot left: 5 descriptors × 32 B = 160 B moved
clear bit 4 and shift five order bytes: 5 B moved; the descriptor is left in place and the slot is reusable
In a v1 leaf of 59 entries, an insertion or deletion in the middle shifts about 29 bytes of order[] instead of about 29 × 32 B ≈ 930 B of descriptors;
internal entries (separator KeyRef, child pointer, two CVs) are larger still. Both designs write the new descriptor itself. Reading pays one indirection
(order[rank] → slot), parentRank() scans order[] to recover a rank, and splits still move descriptors between nodes. Physical slots never change
while an entry lives in a node, which is what keeps parentSlot references valid across reorderings.
